_comment: DBE Grade 12 Mathematical Literacy P1, November 2024. Questions + marking-memo
answers extracted by reading the rendered scanned question paper (no text layer)
and the bilingual (Afrikaans/English) Marking Guidelines PDF (text layer present).
Only the ENGLISH memo content is transcribed. solution_method is the method the
MEMO uses to solve each question - this is the content signal the matcher links
against, not the surface wording of the question. memo_answer is verbatim from
the guidelines (decimal commas kept, South African convention).
CONTEXT CONVENTION: Mathematical Literacy questions hang off shared scenario/
resource boxes. The full scenario (tables/graphs/plans described in bracketed
words) is transcribed verbatim inside the text of the FIRST sub-question of each
block, prefixed 'CONTEXT for ...'. Later sub-questions carry a short pointer.
ANNEXURE NOTE: The paper references an ADDENDUM with ANNEXURES A-C (tax table,
store/employee graphs, Indian Union budget pie charts). The addendum PDF is NOT
in this directory; annexure descriptions below are reconstructed from the values
the marking guidelines use, and are marked [ANNEXURE ... - not in repo].
_note_binaries: Both scanned PDFs are committed in this directory (paper1.pdf = question paper, paper1_memo.pdf = bilingual marking guidelines). The addendum (3 annexures) and the loose ANSWER SHEET are not in the repo.

questions.text: CONTEXT for 1.1 (Q1.1.1-1.1.5): School X and School Y conducted an election for new members to serve on the school governing body (SGB). The graph below shows the number of voters voting during different time slots at School X and School Y. [Dual bar graph titled 'NUMBER OF VOTERS PER TIME SLOT AT SCHOOL X AND SCHOOL Y'; vertical axis 'Number of voters' 0-35; horizontal axis has eight time slots. Bars read: 15:00-15:30 School X none / School Y 18; 15:30-16:00 X none / Y 12; 16:00-16:30 X 10 / Y 5; 16:30-17:00 X 12 / Y 9; 17:00-17:30 X 26 / Y 26; 17:30-18:00 X 30 / Y 24; 18:00-18:30 X 18 / Y 5; 18:30-19:00 X 8 / Y 2. Legend: solid = School X, hatched = School Y.] [Adapted from SGB elections, 2024] Use the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Write down the number of voters at School Y from 16:00-16:30.
questions.memo_working: 2A correct number; answer only full marks

questions.text: [Context 1.1: SGB election voters bar graph - see Q1.1.1] Identify the time slot when 30 people voted at School X.
questions.memo_answer: 17:30 - 18:00 (also accepted: 5:30 pm - 6:00 pm; Half past five until 6 o'clock in the afternoon/evening)
questions.memo_working: 1A 17:30 / 5:30 pm / Half past five; 1A 18:00 / 6:00 pm / 6 o'clock

questions.text: [Context 1.1: SGB election voters bar graph - see Q1.1.1] Choose the statement (A-C) below that BEST describes the trend of the voters at School Y. A: As time went by, the voter numbers increased to a maximum and then decreased. B: The voter numbers started high, then decreased and then picked up again. C: The number of voters decreased, then increased and finally decreased with time.
questions.memo_working: 2A correct option

questions.text: [Context 1.1: SGB election voters bar graph - see Q1.1.1] The probability of randomly selecting a voter from School X is 0,56 during the 17:30-18:00 time slot. Write 0,56 as a simplified fraction.
questions.memo_working: 0,56 = 56/100 (1A writing as a fraction) = 14/25 (1A simplification)

questions.text: [Context 1.1: SGB election voters bar graph - see Q1.1.1] Calculate the total number of voters at both schools who voted during the 17:00-17:30 time slot.
questions.topic: Data Handling (reading and adding graph values)
questions.memo_working: Total number = 26 + 26 (1RT correct values, 1MA adding correct values) = 52 (1A simplification)

questions.text: CONTEXT for 1.2 (Q1.2.1-1.2.4): The newly elected SGB planned to have lunch with the staff. TABLE 1 below shows the average comparative food prices for May 2022 and May 2023 needed for some of the lunch items. [TABLE 1: COMPARATIVE FOOD PRICES FOR SOME LUNCH ITEMS. Columns: FOOD ITEMS | PRICE IN RAND (MAY 2022, MAY 2023) | PERCENTAGE CHANGE (YEAR ON YEAR, MONTH ON MONTH). Rows: 410 g beans 12,60 | 15,14 | 20,2 | 0,5; 250 g instant coffee 45,56 | 48,47 | 6,4 | -1,0; Eggs 1,5 dozen tray 52,97 | 57,33 | 8,2 | 1,6; 750 ml sunflower oil 40,68 | 35,52 | -12,7 | -2,3; Oranges per kg 22,07 | 20,10 | -8,9 | -14,5; Chicken giblets per kg 37,73 | 46,75 | 23,9 | 2,2; Chicken portions per 2 kg 86,80 | 93,06 | 7,2 | 0,6; TOTAL: A | R316,37.] [Adapted from www.statsa.gov.za] Use TABLE 1 above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Identify the food items that showed a decrease in both the month-on-month and year-on-year percentage change.
questions.memo_working: 2RT first correct product; 1RT second correct product

questions.text: [Context 1.2: TABLE 1 comparative food prices - see Q1.2.1] Determine the missing value, A.
questions.memo_working: A = R12,60 + R45,56 + R52,97 + R40,68 + R22,07 + R37,73 + R86,80 (1MA adding ALL correct values) = R298,41 (1A simplification, NPU)

questions.text: [Context 1.2: TABLE 1 comparative food prices - see Q1.2.1] Calculate the price of a dozen eggs during May 2022.
questions.memo_working: Price per dozen = R52,97 ÷ 1,5 (1A dividing by 1,5) = R35,31 (1A simplification). OR 1 egg = R52,97/18, x12 = R35,31. OR R52,97/3 = R17,65666 (half dozen), x2 = R35,31. NPR

questions.text: [Context 1.2: TABLE 1 comparative food prices - see Q1.2.1] Write down the unit ratio, in the form 1 : ..., for the price of the oranges in May 2022 to the price of the oranges in May 2023.
questions.memo_working: 22,07 : 20,10 (1RT + 1RT correct values) = 1 : 0,9107385591 ≈ 1 : 0,91 (1A simplification in correct order, NPR)

questions.text: CONTEXT for 1.3 (Q1.3.1-1.3.4): TABLE 2 below gives definitions of terminology used in Mathematical Literacy. [TABLE 2: TERMINOLOGY USED IN MATHEMATICAL LITERACY. A: An increase in the price of a basket of goods or services over time that is representative of the economy as a whole. B: Sum of all the values divided by the number of values. C: The income received from the item sold and the cost price of the item is the same. D: Value or values appearing most often in a data set. E: The difference between the highest and lowest values in a data set. F: An amount paid regularly at a particular rate for the use/loan of money. G: These are amounts that must be paid every month and which stay the same, like rent, school fees and transport costs. H: Middle value in an ordered data set. I: Expenses that change over time or from one week/month to the next, e.g. telephone and electricity costs. J: The point where the income exceeds the expenses.] Use TABLE 2 above and match the definitions with the terminology below. Write only the letter (A-J) next to the question numbers (1.3.1 to 1.3.4), e.g. 1.3.5 K. QUESTION: Break-even point
questions.memo_working: 2A correct letter

questions.text: [Context 1.3: TABLE 2 terminology definitions - see Q1.3.1] Variable expenses
questions.memo_working: 2A correct letter

questions.text: CONTEXT for 2.1 (Q2.1.1-2.1.3): Miecke purchased prepaid electricity and received the following till slip. Note that some information has been omitted. [Till slip: TAX INVOICE VAT NO. 4420106777; *** PREPAID ELECTRICITY ***; Electricity Municipal Prepaid; VAT REGISTRATION NO. 4370102313; Meter: 07032985769; DOMESTIC HOUSEHOLD TARIFF; Transaction Sequence No.: 56332515; Amount R1 300,00; Units *** kWh; Electricity R1 130,43; VAT 15% B; TOTAL R1 300,00.] [Adapted from original till slip] Use the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Write down the meter number.
questions.memo_working: 2RT correct number

questions.text: [Context 2.1: prepaid electricity till slip - see Q2.1.1] Determine the missing value, B.
questions.memo_working: B = R1 300,00 - R1 130,43 (1RT correct value, 1MA subtracting values) = R169,57 (1A simplification). OR B = R1 130,43 x 15/100 = R169,56. OR B = R1 300 x 15/115 = R169,57. AO
questions.memo_note: The memo's second alternative prints R169,56 (0,15 x 1 130,43 = 169,5645 rounded down); the subtraction method gives R169,57. Both appear in the official memo.

questions.text: [Context 2.1: prepaid electricity till slip - see Q2.1.1] A partial residential electricity tariff table (excluding VAT) is shown below. [TABLE 3: RESIDENTIAL ELECTRICITY TARIFF. Block 1: consumption 0-350 kWh, tariff R2,19/kWh; Block 2: consumption more than 350 kWh, tariff R2,91/kWh.] Determine the number of kWh units Miecke purchased.
questions.memo_working: Amount for Block 1 = 350 kWh x R2,19 = R766,50 (1MA, 1CA). Amount left for Block 2 = R1 130,43 - R766,50 = R363,93 (1MCA). Units in Block 2 = R363,93 / R2,91 = 125,0618557 kWh (1MCA, 1CA). Total = 350 kWh + 125,0618557 kWh = 475,06 kWh (1MCA adding, 1CA simplification). OR with VAT-inclusive tariffs: R2,19 x 1,15 = R2,5185 and R2,91 x 1,15 = R3,3465; 350 x R2,5185 = R881,475; R1 300 - R881,475 = R418,525; 418,525/3,3465 = 125,06 kWh; total 475,06 kWh. NPR

questions.text: CONTEXT for 2.2 (Q2.2.1-2.2.3): Miecke plans to install a home solar system unit consisting of solar panels, a battery and an inverter. She sees the advertisement below in a community newspaper showing the two different payment options for the same unit. [HOME SOLAR SYSTEM UNIT PAYMENT OPTIONS. OPTION 1: RENT-TO-OWN - Pay for 7 years at R1 549 p/m; Additional costs: R782 initiation fee; Buy-out after rental period R7 820. OPTION 2: CASH PRICE - R78 200 (incl. VAT).] [Adapted from https://solar.alumo.co.za] Use the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Write down the monthly instalment for the rent-to-own option.
questions.memo_working: 2RT correct amount, NPU

questions.text: [Context 2.2: home solar system payment options - see Q2.2.1] Calculate, excluding VAT, the cash price of the home solar system unit.
questions.memo_working: Price excluding VAT = R78 200 / 1,15 (1RT for R78 200, 1MA dividing by 1,15) = R68 000 (1A simplification). OR R78 200 x 100/115 = R68 000. OR VAT amount = R78 200 x 15/115 ≈ R10 200; R78 200 - R10 200 = R68 000.

questions.text: [Context 2.2: home solar system payment options - see Q2.2.1] After seven years, Miecke decides to buy-out the rent-to-own option. Calculate the extra amount she has to pay compared to buying the home solar system unit for cash.
questions.memo_working: Number of months = 12 x 7 = 84 months (1A). Rent-to-own = (R1 549 x 84) + R782 + R7 820 = R130 116 + R782 + R7 820 (1MCA adding ALL correct values) = R138 718 (1CA). Difference = R138 718 - R78 200 (1MCA subtracting values) = R60 518 (1CA simplification)

questions.text: CONTEXT for 2.3 (Q2.3.1-2.3.2): Miecke is 45 years old and earns a monthly taxable income of R39 275,85 in the 2023/2024 tax year. She does not belong to a medical aid. ANNEXURE A shows the annual tax table for individuals for the 2023/2024 tax year. [ANNEXURE A - not in repo. From the memo it is the SARS 2023/2024 individual income tax table; the bracket used (labelled C) is: taxable income R370 501-R512 800, tax = R77 362 + 31% of taxable income above R370 500; primary rebate R17 235.] Use ANNEXURE A and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Identify the tax bracket that Miecke will use to calculate her income tax payable.
questions.memo_working: Annual taxable income = R39 275,85 x 12 (1MA multiplying by 12) = R471 310,20 (1A simplification). Tax Bracket C (1MCA). AO

questions.text: [Context 2.3: Miecke's income tax, ANNEXURE A tax table - see Q2.3.1] Calculate Miecke's annual tax payable for the 2023/2024 tax year.
questions.memo_working: Tax before rebate = R77 362 + 31%(R471 310,20 - R370 500) (1SF correct substitution) = R77 362 + 31%(R100 810,20) = R77 362 + R31 251,162 (1MCA adding values) = R108 613,162 (1CA). Annual tax payable = R108 613,162 - R17 235 (1RT rebate: R17 235) = R91 378,16 (1CA simplification). CA from Question 2.3.1

questions.text: CONTEXT for 3.1 (Q3.1.1-3.1.4): ANNEXURE B shows two graphs. GRAPH 1 shows the trends in the total number of Shoprite and Pick n Pay stores for the period 2014 to 2023. GRAPH 2 shows the trends in the total number of employees in these two stores for the period 2005 to 2023. [ANNEXURE B - not in repo. Values the memo reads off: in 2023 Shoprite had 3 543 stores and 153 726 employees; Pick n Pay had 2 204 stores and 90 000 employees; the first decrease in Pick n Pay employees was in 2015; in 3 of the 10 years shown (2014-2023) the number of Shoprite stores was fewer than 2 000.] Use ANNEXURE B and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Identify the year in which there was a decrease in the number of employees in the Pick n Pay stores for the first time.
questions.memo_working: 2RT correct year

questions.text: [Context 3.1: ANNEXURE B store/employee graphs - see Q3.1.1] It is projected that the number of Pick n Pay stores will increase by 95,39% from 2023 to 2032. Determine, by means of calculations, the projected number of Pick n Pay stores in 2032.
questions.memo_working: Projected number = 2 204 x 95,39/100 + 2 204 (1RT correct value 2 204, 1MA percentage calculation) = 2 102,3956 + 2 204 = 4 306,3956 = 4 306 (1CA simplification). OR 2 204 x 195,39/100 (or x 1,9539) = 4 306. AO

questions.text: [Context 3.1: ANNEXURE B store/employee graphs - see Q3.1.1] An analyst stated that Shoprite employed more employees per store than Pick n Pay during 2023. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether the analyst's statement is valid.
questions.memo_answer: Shoprite average ≈ 43,39 employees per store; Pick n Pay average ≈ 40,83 employees per store; the statement is VALID.
questions.memo_working: Average Shoprite = 153 726 / 3 543 (1RT 153 726, 1RT 3 543) = 43,388653... employees (1CA). Average Pick n Pay = 90 000 / 2 204 (1RT both correct values) = 40,834845... employees (1CA). Statement is VALID (1O conclusion). NPR

questions.text: [Context 3.1: ANNEXURE B store/employee graphs - see Q3.1.1] Determine, as a percentage, the probability of randomly selecting a year where the number of Shoprite stores is fewer than 2 000.
questions.memo_working: P = 3/10 x 100% (1RT correct numerator, 1RT correct denominator) = 30% (1CA simplification). AO

questions.text: CONTEXT for 3.2 (Q3.2.1-3.2.4): A study relating to the amount of time spent (in minutes) by a selected number of customers in a store was conducted on a particular Saturday. On that Saturday, a total of 12 342 customers visited the store. [Data table, 32 values: 12 15 25 25 40 28 18 23 / 43 15 22 19 15 8 37 9 / 24 23 15 67 25 29 6 17 / 15 43 23 27 33 26 127 10] Use the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Write down the number of customers that represent the sample size and the number of customers that represent the population size for this study.
questions.memo_working: Sample = 32 (1A counting to 32, 1A sample); Population = 12 342 (1A correct population). OR 32 and 12 342 in correct order (no words used)

questions.text: [Context 3.2: time-spent-in-store study - see Q3.2.1] Choose the correct option (A, B, C, D or E) that represents the stage in the data handling process that uses the measures of central tendency and spread. A: Collecting data. B: Classifying and organising data. C: Summarising data. D: Representing data. E: Analysing data.
questions.memo_working: 2A correct option

questions.text: [Context 3.2: time-spent-in-store study - see Q3.2.1] Give a reason why the value of 127 is considered to be an outlier in the data set.
questions.memo_answer: The value 127 is 60 minutes more than the second highest time in the dataset.
questions.memo_working: 2O conclusion

questions.text: [Context 3.2: time-spent-in-store study - see Q3.2.1] Shown below, in rank order, is selected data of the time spent by customers in the store and an incomplete box-and-whisker plot of the same data. [Ranked data, 32 values: 6 8 9 10 12 15 15 15 15 15 17 / 18 19 22 23 23 23 24 25 25 25 26 / 27 28 29 33 37 40 43 43 67 127. Box-and-whisker plot on a 0-140 number line: minimum 6, lower quartile 15, Q3 unlabelled, maximum 127.] Use the information above to answer the questions that follow. (a) Calculate the value of the upper quartile (Q3).
questions.memo_working: Quartile 3 = (28 + 29)/2 (1RT correct values, 1MA concept of quartile) = 28,5 (1CA simplification). AO
questions.memo_note: The ranked list in the question shows 32 values; the memo's Q3 = (28+29)/2 = 28,5 corresponds to the printed data set.

questions.text: [Context 3.2: ranked time data and box-and-whisker plot - see Q3.2.4a] (b) Vuyo stated that if the outlier value was removed from the data set, the new interquartile (IQR) value would be 13. Verify Vuyo's statement, showing ALL calculations.
questions.memo_answer: New Q1 = 15, new Q3 = 28, IQR = 28 - 15 = 13. He is CORRECT.
questions.memo_working: New Quartile 1 = 15 (1RT); New Quartile 3 = 28 (1RT); IQR = Q3 - Q1 (1A correct formula); IQR = 28 - 15 (1MCA subtracting values) = 13; He is CORRECT (1O conclusion)

questions.text: CONTEXT for 4.1 (Q4.1.1-4.1.4): Lee's parents plan to celebrate his 21st birthday. This special event will be held at a popular hotel, starting at 18:00. TABLE 4 below shows some of the budgeted expenses for the party. [TABLE 4: BUDGETED EXPENSES FOR THE PARTY. Cost of the venue: R750 deposit and R6 185 for the day; Food and drinks: R18 000; Birthday cake: R1 250. OPTIONS FOR DISC JOCKEYS (DJs): DJ Rain - R4 000 for 5 hours or less, thereafter the tariff is an additional R1 250 per hour; DJ 5-Star - R1 000 per hour or part thereof; DJ Cool - R6 000 for the party.] [Adapted from www.bloemshowgrounds.co.za>venues & bark.com] Use TABLE 4 and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION 4.1.1: The table below represents the cost to hire DJ Rain. [TABLE 5: COST TO HIRE DJ RAIN PER HOUR. Number of hours: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Cost (in R): 4 000, 4 000, P, 4 000, 4 000, Q, 6 500, 7 750, R.] (a) Write a formula to calculate the cost to hire DJ Rain for more than 5 hours in the following form: Cost = ...
questions.memo_answer: Cost = R4 000 + R1 250 x (number of hours exceeding 5)
questions.memo_working: 1A fixed cost (R4 000); 1A multiply hours with tariff (R1 250); 1A number of hours more than 5. OR Cost = R4 000 + R1 250 x n, where n = number of hours exceeding 5

questions.text: [Context 4.1: birthday party budget, TABLE 5 DJ Rain costs - see Q4.1.1a] (b) Complete the table by calculating the missing values P, Q and R.
questions.topic: Finance (tables of values from a cost model)

questions.text: [Context 4.1: birthday party budget - see Q4.1.1a] The graphs showing the costs to hire DJ 5-Star and DJ Cool are shown on the ANSWER SHEET. [ANSWER SHEET grid 'COMPARISON OF THE COST FOR THE DIFFERENT DJs': cost in rand 0-10 000 vs number of hours playing 0-9; DJ 5-Star plotted as an increasing step graph rising R1 000 per hour; DJ Cool as a horizontal dash-dot line at R6 500.] (a) Name the type of graph used to represent the cost to hire DJ 5-Star.
questions.memo_working: 2A correct name
questions.memo_note: The answer sheet plots DJ Cool as a constant line at R6 500 although TABLE 4 prices DJ Cool at R6 000 for the party; transcribed as printed.

questions.text: [Context 4.1: birthday party budget, TABLE 5 DJ Rain costs - see Q4.1.1a] (b) Use TABLE 5, showing the cost to hire DJ Rain for up to 9 hours, to draw a line graph on the same grid on the ANSWER SHEET.
questions.memo_answer: [Drawn graph] Horizontal line at R4 000 from 0 to 5 hours, then rising straight line to (9; 9 000).
questions.memo_working: CA from 4.1.1(b): 1A starting point (0 ; 4 000); 1A (5 ; 4 000); 1A end point (9 ; 9 000); 1A joining ALL the points plotted on the slanted part of graph

questions.text: [Context 4.1: birthday party budget, TABLE 4 - see Q4.1.1a] Lee's parents decide to hire DJ 5-Star for the 21st birthday party. DJ 5-Star will provide the music entertainment from 18:00 until 01:30. Determine the total budgeted expenses for the party.
questions.memo_working: Time = 18:00 - 01:30 = 7 hrs 30 min ≈ 8 hrs (1A calculating hours). Cost for DJ = 8 x R1 000 (1MCA) = R8 000 (1CA). Total cost = R18 000 + R750 + R6 185 + R1 250 + R8 000 (1MCA adding all values) = R34 185 (1CA simplification)

questions.text: [Context 4.1: birthday party budget, TABLE 4 - see Q4.1.1a] Give ONE reason why Lee's parents did not choose DJ Cool.
questions.memo_answer: He charges a flat/fixed rate, which is not economical if the party ends early. OR He has a bad reputation.
questions.memo_working: 2O correct reason

questions.text: CONTEXT for 4.2 (Q4.2.1-4.2.3): The hotel has three other smaller venues, each accommodating a maximum number of guests per function, as listed below: Cinema-style venue 400 guests; Sit-down venue without dancing space 250 guests; Sit-down venue with dancing space 200 guests. TABLE 6 shows the number of guests accommodated for functions at the three venues during a specific month in 2022 and 2023. [TABLE 6: ACTUAL NUMBER OF GUESTS PER FUNCTION. 2023: 180, 350, 400, 200, 215, 90, 150, 230, 160. 2022: 360, 160, 300, 70, 160, 200, 240.] [Adapted from www.bloemshowgrounds.co.za>venues] Use TABLE 6 and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Write, as a decimal, the probability that a cinema-style venue was chosen as a suitable function venue for all the functions held during 2022 and 2023.
questions.memo_working: P = 4/16 (1A numerator, 1A denominator) = 0,25 (1CA simplification)
questions.memo_note: Numerator 4 = functions with more than 250 guests (only the cinema-style venue could host them: 350, 400 in 2023; 360, 300 in 2022); denominator 16 = total functions.

questions.text: [Context 4.2: venue guest numbers, TABLE 6 - see Q4.2.1] Determine the median number of guests accommodated during 2023.
questions.memo_working: Arranged: 90 150 160 180 200 215 230 350 400 (1A arranging); Median = 200 (2A median). AO

questions.text: [Context 4.2: venue guest numbers, TABLE 6 - see Q4.2.1] The manager stated that the range of the number of guests per function during 2022, is the same as the range of the number of guests per function during 2023. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is valid.
questions.memo_answer: Range 2022 = 360 - 70 = 290; Range 2023 = 400 - 90 = 310. His statement is NOT VALID.
questions.memo_working: Range 2022 = 360 - 70 (1RT both correct values, 1MCA concept of range) = 290 (1CA). Range 2023 = 400 - 90 = 310 (1A range). NOT VALID (1O conclusion)

questions.text: CONTEXT for 5.1 (Q5.1.1-5.1.5): The pie charts on ANNEXURE C show the Indian Union budgets for income and expenditure for 2023/2024. Some values have been omitted. The currency used in India is the rupee. India also has different denominations for the larger currency amounts. NOTE: 100 000 rupees = 1 lakh; 100 lakhs = 1 crore. [ANNEXURE C - not in repo. From the memo: total budget 45,03 lakh crore. Income pie chart percentages: borrowing 34%; corporation tax 15%; income tax 15%; customs 4%; GST omitted (= 17%); non-debt capital receipts 2%; plus two further sources of 7% and 6%. Expenditure pie chart includes: defence 8%; interest payments 20%.] Use ANNEXURE C and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Choose the correct word from those given in brackets. Write down only the word next to the question number (5.1.1). A budget is a (deficit/surplus/balanced) budget when the income is less than the expenditure.
questions.memo_working: 2A correct word

questions.text: [Context 5.1: Indian Union budget pie charts, ANNEXURE C - see Q5.1.1] General sales tax (GST) is a tax that is similar to VAT in South Africa. Calculate the missing percentage for GST on the pie chart.
questions.memo_working: GST % = 100% - (15% + 15% + 4% + 7% + 6% + 2% + 34%) (1RT ALL correct values, 1MA adding and subtracting) = 100% - 83% = 17% (1CA simplification). AO

questions.text: [Context 5.1: Indian Union budget pie charts, ANNEXURE C - see Q5.1.1] Calculate, in lakh crores, the amount spent on defence in India.
questions.memo_working: Defence = 8% x 45,03 lakh crore (1RT correct percentage, 1MA multiply by 45,03) = 3,6024 lakh crore (1CA simplification). NPR, AO

questions.text: [Context 5.1: Indian Union budget pie charts, ANNEXURE C - see Q5.1.1] List THREE sources of income shown on the pie chart where the total percentages add up to the borrowing percentage value.
questions.memo_answer: Corporation tax + Income tax + Customs (15% + 15% + 4% = 34%). OR Corporation tax + GST + Non Debt Capital Receipts (15% + 17% + 2% = 34%). OR Income tax + GST + Non Debt Capital Receipts (15% + 17% + 2% = 34%).
questions.memo_working: 1RT correct source; 1RT correct source; 1RT correct source adding to 34%. CA from 5.1.2 for GST

questions.text: [Context 5.1: Indian Union budget pie charts, ANNEXURE C - see Q5.1.1] Sanji calculated, in lakh crores, the amount spent on interest payments. He rounded off his answer to the nearest whole number. Sanji stated that the rounded answer he calculated did not make much difference in rupees when compared to the non-rounded answer. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is valid.
questions.memo_answer: Interest payments = 20% x 45,03 = 9,006 lakh crore; unrounded = 90 060 000 rupees; rounded (9 lakh crore) = 90 000 000 rupees; difference = 60 000 rupees. His statement is NOT VALID.
questions.memo_working: Interest payments = 20% x 45,03 lakh crore (1RT both correct values) = 9,006 lakh crore (1A). Unrounded = 9,006 x 100 x 100 000 = 90 060 000 rupees (1C conversion). Rounded = 9 x 100 x 100 000 (1R) = 90 000 000 rupees. Difference = 60 000 rupees (1CA). NOT VALID (1O conclusion). OR difference 9,006 - 9,000 = 0,006 lakh crore = 60 000 rupees.

questions.text: CONTEXT for 5.2 (Q5.2.1-5.2.2): In 2024, South Africa received R302,4 billion from corporate income tax. NOTE: R1 000 000 = 4 447 989,1 rupees; 4 447 989,1 rupees = 44,479891 lakhs. [Adapted from www.wise.com/, 10 June 2024] QUESTION: Convert R302,4 billion to million rands.
questions.memo_working: R302,4 billion x 1 000 (1MA multiplying by 1 000) = R302 400 million (1A simplification). AO

questions.text: [Context 5.2: SA corporate income tax and rand-rupee conversion - see Q5.2.1] Hence, convert the South African corporate income tax to lakh crore.
questions.memo_working: R302 400 million = R302 400 x 44,479891 lakh (1MA multiplying by correct exchange rate) = 13 450 719,04 lakh (1CA) = 13 450 719,04 / 100 (1MCA dividing by 100) = 134 507,1904 lakh crore (1CA simplification). NPR. CA from Question 5.2.1

questions.text: CONTEXT for 5.3 (Q5.3.1-5.3.2): A house in Chennai, India, is valued at 5 000 000 rupees at the end of 2024. TABLE 7 shows the inflation rates in India for house prices for the last five years. [TABLE 7: INFLATION RATES IN INDIA FOR THE LAST FIVE YEARS. 2024: 8%; 2023: 7,5%; 2022: 7%; 2021: 6,5%; 2020: 6%.] [Adapted from hewire.in/economy/the-truth-about-inflation-in-india-and-around-the-world] Use TABLE 7 and the information above to answer the questions that follow. QUESTION: Describe the trend in the inflation rates in India.
questions.memo_answer: As the years increase the inflation rate increases. OR The inflation rate increases from 2020 to 2024.
questions.memo_working: 1O years increase; 1O rate increases

questions.text: [Context 5.3: Chennai house value and TABLE 7 inflation rates - see Q5.3.1] Calculate how much the house was worth at the end of 2022.
questions.memo_working: Price at end of 2023 = 5 000 000 / 1,08 (1A 1,08 or 108%, 1MA dividing) = 4 629 629,63 rupees (1CA). Price at end of 2022 = 4 629 629,63 / 1,075 (1MCA 1,075 or 107,5%, 1MA dividing) = 4 306 632,214 rupees (1CA simplification). OR 5 000 000 x 100/108 x 100/107,5 = 4 306 632,214 rupees. NPU, NPR
